assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Each policy threshold (650 for non-seniors, 600 for seniors) is verifiable from the table via boundary rows or a policy column.
assertions.evidence: 'At the standard threshold, not above it | 40 | 650 ... REJECTED' paired with '651 ... APPROVED'; likewise 600/601 for seniors.

assertions.text: Cell values use concrete domain terms, not abstract codes.
assertions.evidence: '40 | 650 | true | REJECTED' and '651 | true | APPROVED' use concrete ages, scores, and named outcomes.

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario"

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions, not outcomes.
assertions.evidence: 'Just above the standard threshold', 'Qualifying score with unstable income' describe conditions, not just 'Approved'/'Rejected'.

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language.
assertions.evidence: Header row: 'Scenario | Age | Credit Score | Stable Income | Result?'

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Decision?' or 'Status?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Result?

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 1 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 1 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Distinct concerns are each covered without a monolithic cross-multiplied table.
assertions.evidence: Single table with rows grouped by concern (threshold pairs, income variation rows) rather than a full age x score x income cross-product.

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed, no re-covering of an already-proven rule.
assertions.evidence: 'Senior qualifying score with missing income information | 70 | 610 | | PENDING_REVIEW' duplicates the income-null rule already shown by row 8 at 40/700, and rows 3-4 ('Not yet senior...' / 'Senior age boundary...') re-demonstrate the age-effect already shown by the threshold boundary pairs (rows 1-2 vs 5-6).

assertions.text: Age boundary, credit score categorisation, and income status are each covered by minimal scenarios.
assertions.evidence: Rows 1-6 cover age/credit boundaries; rows 7-9,11 cover income status (false, null) at qualifying and below-threshold scores.

assertions.text: Scenario names and @Description do not restate values already shown in the table.
assertions.evidence: Description states policy thresholds ('approved above a credit score of 650', 'lower threshold of 600') which are policy values, not pinned single-row input restatements.

assertions.text: Effect of stable income is visible via a held-constant row pair.
assertions.evidence: '40 | 700 | false | REJECTED' vs '40 | 700 | | PENDING_REVIEW' hold age/score constant while income differs, yielding different decisions.

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable.
assertions.evidence: Result column varies across REJECTED, APPROVED, PENDING_REVIEW depending on inputs, e.g. '651 | true | APPROVED' vs '650 | true | REJECTED'.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body.
assertions.evidence: @Description explicitly states thresholds: "approved above a credit score of 650... senior applicants (age 65+) are approved above a lower threshold of 600. The senior age cutoff is inclusive at 65." and precedence/pending assumptions are also stated in the description, matching the table rows.

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName (or the method name it falls back to) states what the code under test does, not an external fact it depends on.
assertions.evidence: Method name `evaluatesLoanApproval` describes the action performed by the code (evaluating loan approval), not a restated domain fact.

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: A value the rule's outcome depends on, held constant for every row, must be visible as a column or named in the @DisplayName/@Description.
assertions.evidence: The thresholds (650, 600, 65) are explicitly declared in @Description: "approved above a credit score of 650... lower threshold of 600... senior age cutoff is inclusive at 65", satisfying the requirement rather than hiding them in code.
